text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nicosia accuses the Turks of imagining an incident at Louroujina yesterday in which shots were fired.
- Industrialists express satisfaction with government measures to support them.
- The United Nations launches a probe into mystery shots fired in Louroujina.
- Industrialists give a cautious welcome to the government's export aid package.
- Opposition parties express concern over billion-pound defence spending.
- Government defence spending plans over the next five years are excessive, says Communist Akel party leader Demetris Christofias.
- Consultations among opposition parties intensify to find a presidential candidate to run in the 1998 presidential race.
- Cyprus's economic climate is improving. The Cyprus Stock Exchange index starts to rise.
- Plumbers are in high demand after pipes and water tanks cracked from the cold weather.
- Explosive climate prevails in conference of secondary school teachers union called to examine working conditions, the state payroll and juvenile delinquency.
